title: GELU Compiler output loses its libdevice dependency at common build admission

evidence.note: The GELU forward and backward task baselines failed in the common Triton build path. Other tasks had already consumed provider tokens before the matrix reached these baselines. Their original workspaces and failures remain unchanged.

The public CPU replay reproduces both failures: Compiler lowering is eligible and emits the explicit libdevice import, but project_triton_kernel reports unsupported call. The first repair restored both positive paths; independent review then found module/function values escaping through the generic tensor .to rule, which was repaired in 26eb4d98 and passed 24 independent CPU probes. The first positive replay is not approval of that superseded admission boundary.

Independent review rebuilt the exact v76 Gate with all 124 cases matched and 175 bound sources before authoring the separate release approval. The previously released native v75 authority was preserved before the canonical cycle derived v76.

observation: The Triton backend already emits the declared libdevice.tanh.f32 operation, but project_triton_kernel discarded its import and validate_triton_kernel refused the call even with the explicit import present. This is an inconsistency between Compiler lowering and its common build interface, rather than a missing GELU primitive. The returned first repair also showed that naming an allowed attribute is insufficient when the module or function object can escape to another consumer.
proposed_change: Preserve only the exact canonical optional libdevice import and admit only direct libdevice.tanh calls. Require the module name to be the receiver of the tanh attribute and that attribute to be the direct call target; retain casts on the call result. Refuse replacement imports, module/function aliases, reserved-name shadowing and other libdevice calls. Implementation commits d037369d and 26eb4d98 are integrated as 81f10665 and ff110418. The existing Corpus expectations remain unchanged.
verification_plan: Independent hostile-AST review and a full canonical Corpus Gate bind the corrected source. Replay the failed GELU public projection/admission paths under the released successor, then compile and seal both task baselines through the actual common builder before any new provider campaign. Source/CPU checks alone do not establish GPU correctness or performance.
